newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia finance leaders see 3.7 pct growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Colombia finance leaders see 3.7 pct growth in '97.

text.p: Leaders of Colombia's financial sector are in agreement with Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo that the country is headed for an economic upturn next year, but they expect a lower rate of growth than forecast by the government, an industry association said Thursday.

Armando Montenegro, head of the influential National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF), said the group saw gross domestic product expanding by 3.7 percent in 1997, compared with the government's "conservative" estimate of 4.5 percent growth.
He warned of the continued threat of U.S. economic sanctions in retaliation for what the Clinton administration views as Colombia's failure to step up its fight against drug trafficking.
Montenegro also cautioned that the second half of 1997 could bring fresh political turmoil amid the build-up to the 1998 presidential elections.

Still, the association's 3.7 percent forecast is an upward revision from an earlier estimate of 2.0 percent growth in 1997. And Montenegro did not rule out a rise of as much as 5.0 percent, pointing out that an economic decline was often followed by a boom.

The association's 1997 forecast is based on an assumption of 3 percent growth in banking, agriculture and business and an increase in oil production to 717,000 barrels a day in 1997 from 630,000 barrels a day this year

In addition, possible cuts in interest rates, the prospect of an upturn in trade with neighbouring Venezuela and a continued influx of foreign investment could all contribute to stronger growth next year, Montenegro said.
